supporting_observations.claim: At 13:22 UTC, ruth.moss launched mmc.exe with dsa.msc, the Active Directory Users and Computers console; the process was recorded at high integrity.
That MMC process connected from WS-RMOSS-01 to 10.54.20.10 on ports 135 and 389, consistent with communication to a domain controller for directory administration.

The available records do not show whether c.rwong was created, who created it, or what groups or privileges it received; the observed console launch and directory connections alone do not establish those actions.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records contain no explicit directory account-creation or account-change event for c.rwong.
The records show directory-console activity and connections, but not the actions performed within the console or the resulting account configuration.
claims_not_established: Whether c.rwong was created at approximately 13:42 UTC as stated in the alert.
Whether ruth.moss created the account, or whether any other actor did.
Whether c.rwong was placed only in the Seasonal group or received any unauthorized privileges.
Whether the account creation was authorized under a specific request or change.
additional_evidence_needed: Domain controller security and directory-service audit events for account creation and group membership changes involving c.rwong during the alert window.
The account's creation timestamp, creator/subject identity, group memberships, and privilege-related attributes from the directory.
The help-desk request or approval associated with the temporary account, if one exists.
unrelated_findings: Ruth.moss's browser accessed slack.com and Slack asset endpoints during the review window; this is separate from the account-management alert and may warrant a policy review because Slack is not listed in the supplied approved-services inventory.
